unit.title: E-commerce: margins, baskets and feeds
unit.description: AOV, conversion rate, cart abandonment, repeat purchase, RFM, product feeds, Merchant Center, contribution margin

cards.definition: Revenue = sessions x conversion rate x average order value. Each lever has its own tactics: traffic (SEO, ads), conversion (UX, trust, offer) and basket (bundles, thresholds, cross-sell).
cards.example: 100,000 sessions x 2 percent x 60 euros = 120,000 euros. Raising AOV to 66 euros adds 12,000 euros with the same traffic.

cards.definition: Offering free delivery above an amount set slightly above the current average order value, to push buyers to add one more item.
cards.example: AOV is 42 euros: free shipping from 50 euros encourages a small extra item.

cards.definition: Cross-sell suggests a complementary product (a case with a phone); upsell suggests a better, pricier version of the same product (the 256 GB model).
cards.example: Frequently bought together blocks are cross-sell; upgrade for 50 euros more is upsell.

exercises.prompt: A shop has 50,000 sessions, a 2 percent conversion rate and an AOV of 80 euros. What is its revenue?
exercises.explain: 50,000 x 0.02 = 1,000 orders, x 80 euros = 80,000 euros. Every lever of the equation multiplies the others.

exercises.prompt: You took 20,000 euros from 400 orders today. What is the AOV?
exercises.explain: Average order value = revenue divided by orders. Track it with the margin: a bigger basket full of discounts is not always better.

exercises.prompt: Your AOV is 45 euros. Where do you set the free shipping threshold?
exercises.explain: Just above the AOV nudges many buyers to add one item. Too low gives margin away; too high motivates nobody.

exercises.prompt: A buyer adds a camera to the cart and is offered a memory card. What is it?
exercises.explain: Cross-sell adds a complementary product. Upsell would offer a better camera.

exercises.prompt: Out of 1,000 carts created, 300 become orders. What is the cart abandonment rate?
exercises.explain: 700 abandoned divided by 1,000. Typical causes: surprise shipping costs, forced account creation, slow checkout.

exercises.prompt: In an RFM analysis, what do the three letters stand for?
exercises.explain: RFM ranks customers on how recently, how often and how much they buy, to target champions, loyal buyers and those at risk.

exercises.prompt: What do you need to run Google Shopping ads?
choices: A product feed sent to Google Merchant Center
A YouTube channel with product videos
A physical shop open to the public
exercises.explain: Shopping ads are built from the feed: titles, prices, images and stock. Feed quality drives ad performance.

exercises.prompt: A sale with a high revenue can lose money once product cost, shipping, fees and ad cost are deducted.
exercises.explain: True. Contribution margin per order is what pays the bills. ROAS alone can hide unprofitable sales.

exercises.prompt: A marketplace announces a GMV of 50 million euros. What does it measure?
choices: The total value of goods sold through it
The commission revenue it keeps for itself
Its net profit after all its costs
The money invested by its shareholders
exercises.explain: GMV counts what buyers paid sellers. The platform revenue is only the commission on it.

exercises.title: A fashion shop with thin margins
exercises.scenario: An online clothing shop: 3 percent conversion, AOV 38 euros, shipping costs 6 euros per order, ROAS on ads at 4.

steps.prompt: ROAS is 4, but the shop barely makes money. Why?
choices: After product cost, shipping, returns and fees, little margin is left
A ROAS of 4 always means a strong profit
The conversion rate of 3 percent is too high
steps.feedback: With a 50 percent gross margin, 4 euros of revenue per euro of ads leaves 2 euros, before shipping, returns and fees. Check the break-even ROAS.

steps.prompt: Which move raises profit without buying more traffic?
choices: Free shipping from 50 euros plus outfit bundles
A permanent minus 40 percent on everything
Doubling the ad budget at the same ROAS
Removing all product photos to load faster
steps.feedback: Raising the AOV spreads the fixed shipping cost over a bigger basket. Permanent discounts would destroy the margin.

steps.prompt: Returns are at 35 percent. What do you try first?
choices: Better size guides, fit reviews and real photos on models
Charging every customer 20 euros per return
Hiding the returns policy deep in the site
Stopping all sales of trousers and dresses
steps.feedback: Most fashion returns come from fit and expectation gaps. Fix the information before adding friction.

exercises.explain: Look past revenue: margin per order, basket size and returns decide whether e-commerce makes money.
